blocks.content: A Job runs a Pod until it completes successfully, then stops, a fundamentally different goal from a Deployment, which keeps its Pods running indefinitely.

Every workload type covered so far in this course, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, is meant to keep its Pods running continuously. A Job has the opposite goal, run the Pod, let it finish its work, and then be done.

blocks.alt: A finite goal, unlike every long-running workload type covered before this

blocks.content:
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-migration
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: migration-tool:1.0
      restartPolicy: Never

codes.yaml:

kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-migration
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: migration-tool:1.0
      restartPolicy: Never

blocks.content: A Job actively tracks how many of its Pods have completed successfully, this bookkeeping is exactly what lets it know when its work is genuinely done, distinct from just having a Pod that happens to still be running.

blocks.alt: Real bookkeeping of success, not just whether a Pod is currently alive

blocks.content: If a Job's Pod fails, it is not simply abandoned, the Job retries it, up to a configurable backoffLimit, covered in full in the Completion Policy topic later in this module, giving transient failures a real chance to succeed on a retry.

blocks.alt: A real retry mechanism, not giving up after a single failure

blocks.content: This connects directly to the restartPolicy topic from the Pods module, a Deployment expects Always, running forever, a Job typically uses OnFailure or Never, precisely because it is meant to run once and then genuinely be finished.

blocks.alt: Forever and self-healing versus once, then genuinely done

blocks.content: A one-off database migration script, run exactly once against production, is a textbook Job use case, something that needs to run to completion reliably, with retry protection, but should never run indefinitely like an ordinary service.

blocks.alt: A one-off task, run reliably to completion, exactly what a Job is built for

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Job runs a Pod to completion and then stops, the opposite goal from every long-running workload type covered earlier in this course.
It tracks successful completions and retries failures up to a configurable limit, the right tool for reliable, one-off batch work.
